/-!
# Erdős Problem 431

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/431](https://www.erdosproblems.com/431)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos431

open scoped Pointwise

/-- Are there two infinite sets $A$ and $B$ such that $A+B$ agrees with the primes up to finitely
many exceptions? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_431 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧
      (A + B : Set ℕ) =ᶠ[Filter.cofinite] {n | n.Prime} := by
  sorry

end Erdos431

reformulations.difference: The source’s agreement “up to finitely many exceptions” is expressed using eventual equality of sets along Filter.cofinite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For sets viewed as predicates, eventual equality means membership is equivalent outside a finite set. Thus the Lean condition is exactly finiteness of the symmetric difference of A + B and the primes. Since the ground type is ℕ, it is also equivalent to ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ((∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a + b = n) ↔ n.Prime). Both equivalences, including the surrounding existential quantifiers and infinitude requirements, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited page’s existence question. Both infinitude requirements are conjoined under the existential quantifiers, and answer(sorry) has the appropriate propositional type and scope. Lean checks confirmed ordinary pointwise addition, exclusion of empty and singleton summands, and non-vacuity of the cofinite filter on ℕ; small sumsets and primality values were also tested. The live source returned a Cloudflare challenge, so its wording and remarks were read from an archived copy. The current public database still records problem 431 as open, consistent with the recent primary literature. No mathematical defect or status discrepancy was found.
